payload.title: Thu 12/3: The Saturday track
payload.purpose: Saturday 10:00 to 1:00 for people whose week has no room.

captions.LI:
The Bariatric Counseling Center runs an Intensive Outpatient Program with multiple tracks each week. One of those is Saturday morning, 10:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m.

For people whose weekday schedules have no room, the Saturday track offers the same full program: behavioral therapy and counseling, dietary guidance and support, culinary classes, and mindful movement. One program, not four.

The program runs about three months and roughly 30 sessions, meeting two to three times per week. Patients attend the track that fits their schedule. Virtual and on-site options are available.

The staff is comprised of a clinical psychologist, licensed professional counselors, registered dietitians, movement therapists, and a registered nurse, as well as a professional chef. We coordinate care with referring providers and provide progress notes as requested.

We accept most health insurances. Patients typically attend for little to no cost.

San Antonio and virtual across Texas.

#BehavioralHealth

payload.title: Mon 12/7: What intuitive eating means here
payload.purpose: Intuitive Eating as taught in the program, with a clinical psychologist and registered dietitians in the room.

captions.FB: Intuitive eating is a core part of the program at the Bariatric Counseling Center. It's taught by a clinical psychologist and registered dietitians working together in the same room. That's different from learning it from a book or a single practitioner. You learn to notice hunger and fullness cues without rigid rules. You explore why certain foods feel forbidden and practice making choices that feel right for your body. The team helps you work through the emotions that come up around food. This is behavioral therapy, dietary guidance, and mindful eating happening at once. One program, not four. San Antonio and virtual across Texas. Link in the first comment.

At the Bariatric Counseling Center, we help clients understand the connections between sleep, stress, and eating patterns. Our program includes behavioral therapy, dietary guidance, culinary classes, and mindful movement. One program, not four.

We serve San Antonio and virtual across Texas.

payload.title: Tue 12/15: Referring providers: weight loss medications and the behavioral half
payload.purpose: Patients on weight loss medications (never the drug class abbreviation): the habits that keep the result. Document post.

captions.LI:
Patients on weight loss medications often see meaningful physical changes, but sustaining those results requires addressing the behavioral patterns that made weight management difficult in the first place.

At the Bariatric Counseling Center, we provide comprehensive behavioral treatment for obesity that works alongside medical interventions. Our intensive outpatient program helps patients build the skills needed to maintain their progress: understanding and modifying their relationship with food, developing sustainable eating patterns, and creating movement routines they can continue long after medication ends.

The program can be standalone behavioral treatment for obesity, or in addition to bariatric surgery or weight loss medication that patients receive from their medical providers. We accept most health insurances, with claims processed under patients' mental health benefits.

Our team coordinates care with referring medical providers and, at patient discharge, we give referring providers a detailed summary of the patient's behavioral progress during the time in our intensive outpatient program. Progress notes as requested, typically within two business days.

Serving patients both onsite in San Antonio and virtually throughout Texas. Our Director of Admissions is Leloni Gonzales: lgonzales@bccsanantonio.com or 210-634-2200.

#BehavioralHealth
captions.GBP:
Patients on weight loss medications benefit from behavioral support that addresses the habits behind lasting results. At the Bariatric Counseling Center, we provide comprehensive behavioral treatment for obesity that works alongside medical interventions prescribed by referring providers.

Our intensive outpatient program includes group and individual therapy, dietary guidance, cooking classes, chef-prepared meals, mindful eating and movement education in a unique, all-inclusive format. The staff is comprised of a clinical psychologist, licensed professional counselors, registered dietitians, movement therapists, and a registered nurse, as well as a professional chef. One program, not four.

The program can be standalone behavioral treatment for obesity, or in addition to bariatric surgery or weight loss medication that patients receive from their medical providers. We coordinate care with referring providers and provide detailed discharge summaries. Progress notes as requested.

Patients typically attend for little to no cost, with claims processed under mental health benefits. San Antonio and virtual across Texas.

Our staff is comprised of a clinical psychologist, licensed professional counselors, registered dietitians, movement therapists, and a registered nurse, as well as a professional chef.
